S1.why: Number plus adjective is how a German label marks slots; 'kostenlos' is the one word for free used on every key, so the bracket and the subtitle agree.

S2.why: An invitation that points at the waiting dashed tile; no limit word like 'Limit' or 'voll', so it cannot read as a warning.

S3.s: Du nutzt alle %lld kostenlosen Cutlings. Sie bleiben kostenlos und funktionieren weiter.
S3.back: You use all 5 free Cutlings. They stay free and work further.
S3.why: Present tense 'Du nutzt' is how a German says a quota is in use; after 'Du' the capital 'Sie' can only be 'they'; 'kostenlos' is repeated on purpose because staying free is the point.

S4.why: German puts the number first to stress it; this word order is how a native would say it aloud, not 'Du kannst ... speichern'.

S5.why: Same frame as S3 so the three subtitles read as one voice; 'von' joins the pair and works for 1 too, so no plural form is needed; the numbers keep English order, so no positional forms.

S6.why: A noun phrase like the other bold lines; 'Cutlings' is the vocabulary's plural, and the app gives the number already formatted as 5.000.

S7.s: Du kannst %@ Texte und %lld Bilder speichern.
S7.back: You can 5.000 texts and 500 images save.
S7.why: 'Texte' and 'Bilder' are the vocabulary's words for the two kinds; the verb goes last, which is German sentence order.

S8.why: A German list of three takes no comma before 'und'.

S9.s: Ein Kauf gilt für alle Geräte mit deinem Apple-Account.
S9.back: One purchase counts for all devices with your Apple-Account.
S9.why: 'Geräte mit deinem Apple-Account' is the phrase the vocabulary's sync sentence already uses, hyphen included; 'gilt für' is how Germans say a ticket or licence covers something.

S10.why: Spoken German for 'pay once and that is it'; lower-case 'fertig' here is the everyday 'done with', which is different from the Fertig button.

S11.s: Kein Abo, keine Werbung, keine Registrierung.
S11.back: No subscription, no advertising, no registration.
S11.why: 'Abo' is the everyday word for a subscription; 'Registrierung' is signing up, and it avoids 'Anmeldung', which also means logging in.

S12.why: The standard wording German iOS apps use for the App Store restore action.

S13.why: A subjectless passive is how German UI shows a process; Apple's German puts a space before the ellipsis, as Duden does when it stands for left-out words.

S14.why: 'einmalig' in front of a price is how German shops print a one-off charge; 'freischalten' is the German verb for unlocking an app; with the price left out it is 26 characters.

S15.why: The same verb as S14 without the price; a German button is an infinitive.

S16.why: The usual German way to put something off politely; it does not refuse.

S17.why: The label iOS uses for its close buttons in German.

S18.why: Warm and a little proud, and it says 'everything' without listing it; 'deins' keeps the du address.

S19.s: Danke. Dein Kauf hilft Cutling und dem einen Menschen dahinter.
S19.back: Thanks. Your purchase helps Cutling and the one human behind-it.
S19.why: A short 'Danke.' first, the way a person says it; 'Mensch' has no gender, so it fits whoever builds the app.

S20.s: Willkommen zurück. Dein Kauf ist wieder da.
S20.back: Welcome back. Your purchase is again there.
S20.why: 'wieder da' is warmer than the technical 'wiederhergestellt', which the link already used.

S21.why: VoiceOver gets a short state, without a sentence frame; it uses the same words as S5.

S22.why: The count goes against 'Plätzen', so the line is grammatical for 1, 2, 5 and 21 with no plural form; 'Platz' is the room word from S2.

S23.s: Cutling ist freigeschaltet. Platz für %@ Cutlings.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. Room for 5.000 Cutlings.
S23.why: The state first, then the room, in the words S2 and S6 already use.

S24.why: A participle title, the way German alerts name a state; it blames nobody.

S25.s: Der App Store ist gerade nicht erreichbar. Versuch es gleich noch einmal.
S25.back: The App Store is right-now not reachable. Try it shortly once more.
S25.why: 'nicht erreichbar' is the standard German phrase; 'Versuch es gleich noch einmal' is the du imperative for 'try again shortly'.

S26.s: Der App Store hat diesen Kauf nicht bestätigt.
S26.back: The App Store has this purchase not confirmed.
S26.why: It names what happened and nothing else; the perfect tense is how a German reports a past event in speech.

S27.s: Mit dem Apple-Account auf diesem Gerät wurde Cutling noch nicht gekauft.
S27.back: With the Apple-Account on this device was Cutling not yet bought.
S27.why: A passive puts the account in front and blames nobody; 'noch nicht' is softer than 'nie'.

S28.s: Die kostenlose Version fasst %lld Cutlings. Einmal freigeschaltet, speichert Cutling beliebig viele.
S28.back: The free version holds 5 Cutlings. Once unlocked, saves Cutling any-number many.
S28.why: 'fassen' is the German verb for how much a container holds; the leading 'Einmal freigeschaltet' carries both 'once' and 'unlocked' in two words; 'beliebig viele' is the everyday 'as many as you like'; 97 characters with the number.

S29.why: A label-and-value pair fits 18 characters; '4 von 5 kostenlos' on its own could be read as four slots left.

K1.why: The string has one number, so 'alle' says full; 'Plätze' is the slot word from S22; a German verb on its own after the dot reads as a link; 'kostenlos' is dropped to fit 38 characters, and the person has just tried to save a sixth item, so the meaning is clear.

M1.why: A German Mac command title is object plus infinitive, like 'Software aktualisieren'.

M2.why: The same command as a button that opens a window; Apple's German menus and buttons put a space before the ellipsis.

M3.why: A noun-phrase row label in the vocabulary's plural; its value comes from M4.

M4.why: 'von' is how German writes a pair compactly; '3/5' would read as a date or a fraction.

M5.why: The participle as a status, the way German settings show a state.

M6.s: Ein Kauf schaltet Cutling auf iPhone, iPad und Mac frei.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac free.
M6.why: The separable verb goes around the object as German does; the list uses S8.

M7.s: Auf iPhone, iPad und Mac mit diesem Apple-Account freigeschaltet.
M7.back: On iPhone, iPad and Mac with this Apple-Account unlocked.
M7.why: A participle at the end makes a status line with no subject; 'Apple-Account' is the vocabulary's spelling.

M8.s: Du hast Cutling gekauft, bevor es kostenlos wurde. Es bleibt freigeschaltet. Danke dafür.
M8.back: You have Cutling bought, before it free became. It stays unlocked. Thanks for-that.
M8.why: Three short plain facts and then the thanks; 'Danke dafür' ties the thanks to the purchase without gushing.
